text:
sanjay (eng-runtime): ran a multi-gpu chaosbench this morning: trying adaptive prefetch + adaptive batching vs eager/none across H100/A100/L40S. posting quick notes and numbers.

tess: nice, short summary pls? :eyes:

sanjay (eng-runtime): TL;DR: adaptive prefetch + batch heuristics reduces kv-cache thrash at long seqs, but adds p95 variance for small-batch low-latency cases. eager prefetch gives best throughput if memory fits, but catastrophically thrashes when paged-KV spills happen (seq >= 4096 on our configs).

luke: did you test with the fused-paged variant and the new tiling kernel?

sanjay (eng-runtime): yes. kernels tested: flash-fused-v2, paged-flash, fused-paged-tiling. bench script:
```
./bench_runner \n  --gpu h100 \n  --kernel fused-paged-tiling \n  --seq 4096 \n  --batch 2 \n  --kv-prefetch eager \n  --iters 200
```
results (sample rows):
```
GPU   seq   batch  kernel                 prefetch   p50(ms)  p95(ms)  tokens/s
H100  512    1    flash-fused-v2        adaptive   22       40       12.3k
H100  4096   2    paged-flash           eager      210      480      5.1k  (KV thrash spikes)
L40S  1024   4    flash-fused-v2        none       75       200      3.8k
A100  2048   1    fused-paged-tiling    adaptive   120      260      6.0k
```
Notes: p95 for eager/paged at long seqs includes multiple OOM-recover/backpressure events which inflate latency. adaptive prefetch moved many of those into longer but more stable tails.

anya: where are the full traces/artifacts?

infra-bot: perf-run completed, artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/chaosbench/2067008888/ (cpu/gpu traces, metrics CSV, flamegraphs)

morgan: can you attach a minimal repro? we need something small to run in CI perf harness.

sanjay (eng-runtime): minimal repro (script) below — essentially run with model sharded small (6B) and these flags: 
```
PYTHONPATH=./bench ./bench_runner \n  --model small-6B \n  --gpu a100 \n  --kernel paged-flash \n  --seq 4096 \n  --batch 1 \n  --kv-prefetch eager \n  --collect-trace \n  --iters 50
```
I also pushed the perf branch: git@github.com:redwood/inference.git:perf/kv-prefetch-adaptive — bench harness + perf-config in perf/benchmarks.

luke: quick thought — maybe lower the adaptive prefetch aggressiveness threshold (default 0.7) and bump the batch-gain floor so we don't swap a tiny p50 for huge p95. can you run a quick sweep with thresholds 0.4/0.6/0.8?

sanjay (eng-runtime): will do. scheduling sweeps now, starting with thresholds [0.4,0.6,0.8] across H100/A100. will post updated CSVs.

anya: also check kv-cache hit/miss ratio per-request in traces — helps to correlate latency spikes.

sanjay (eng-runtime): yup, collected per-request kv hit/miss in metrics CSV. early look: eager on H100@4096 -> miss rate ~18% causing mem spill cycles; adaptive -> miss rate ~6% but avg token latency +5ms.

morgan: make a short RFC? ops + runtime should decide default policy. quick note in #eng-runtime-rfc would be good.

sanjay (eng-runtime): agree. I'll draft a tiny RFC with recommended defaults and a small matrix of when to pick eager vs adaptive vs none. ETA EOD. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: scheduled: perf/sweeps/2067008888-thresholds (H100,A100) — job ids queued.

morgan: thanks — ping when you have the RFC and the final sweep numbers.

sanjay (eng-runtime): will do. linking dashboard where I'll import CSVs: https://perf.redwood/reports/2067008888 (private)
